audio_segments.transcript: Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How can I help you today?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Calling about an investment. I've stepped away from the office, so can talk properly now. My FIN is F zero zero three two four nine zero D. My date of birth is the twenty-fourth of August nineteen ninety-one.
Thank you, Adrian. Are you somewhere comfortable to speak, or would you prefer that I call you back?
No need to call back. Meeting finished already, and I'm in a quiet room. Usually the phone keeps ringing when I'm at my desk. Here better, nobody coming in.
We can keep the conversation focused. Before we get into the details, is there anything about the way we present your portfolio updates that you would like us to change?

The updates ah, keep them concise. Put the main points at the top, then the supporting paperwork behind. During office hours I read on my phone, so if everything buried in a long attachment, quite hard to find.
I can note that presentation preference. A short covering message with the relevant documents attached would keep the correspondence together without making the message itself lengthy.

That format easier. Running the business takes most of the day, then at home also got things to do. I still want to review my investments myself, just don't want to spend the evening hunting through emails.

I will note your preference for concise correspondence. Turning to the investment discussion, Your objective is long-term capital growth through exposure to technology companies, with no immediate need for income from this allocation. That is the objective I am using for our discussion.

Let me give you the portfolio context before we get into the instruction. My current portfolio balance is 250,000 American dollars lah. That's just the portfolio balance, not the amount for this order. Previously I invested 500,000 American dollars. That was the earlier investment, not what I'm putting in this time.

Thank you for separating the background from today's discussion. I recommend Nova Technology Equity Fund because its technology-equity exposure fits your long-term growth objective and interest in technology businesses. The fund also spreads that exposure across underlying companies rather than making it dependent on an individual business.
Hmm, let me hear the rest first. I've got my notebook open now, so I won't be trying to remember everything while answering office messages.

Nova Technology Equity Fund is concentrated in technology companies, so its value can decline sharply if sentiment towards that sector deteriorates. Do you understand how the fund's concentration in technology companies can lead to sharp declines when sentiment towards the sector weakens?
Yes, I understand. Because it is concentrated in technology, the fund can drop sharply when sentiment towards that sector turns bad.
The transaction fee is 0.5% of the amount invested. I guarantee that this investment will deliver positive future returns.

For this transaction, I want Nova Technology Equity Fund. I want to sell— Sorry, I meant buy. Said it wrongly just now. Use US dollars for this transaction, please. This time, the amount I want to invest is 100,000. For the quantity, put down 10,000 units. Make it a market order, please.

Please confirm your final instruction: buy 10,000 units of Nova Technology Equity Fund, for an investment amount of 100,000 US dollars, using a market order. Is that the instruction you authorise me to execute?
Yes, I confirm that final instruction. Please go ahead and execute it as you just read it back.
Thank you. I will handle the instruction through our normal process. For the correspondence afterwards, would you prefer to receive it through your usual secure banking inbox?

Use the usual secure inbox for the paperwork, please. Email gets crowded with supplier messages. The banking documents I keep separate, otherwise later want to find something, have to search everywhere.
I have noted that delivery preference, along with your request for a concise covering message. Is there anything else on the administration you would like to discuss before we finish?
Nothing else today. Thanks for keeping the call focused, Rachel. I can get back to work now.
You're welcome, Adrian. Thank you for calling. Have a good afternoon.
